papers.title: Process Optimization and Microstructural Evolution of TC4 Alloy with YH2 Addition Fabricated by PBF-LB
papers.abstract: A three-factor, four-level orthogonal design was employed to optimize the overall forming quality of powder bed fusion with a laser beam (PBF-LB)-fabricated TC4 alloy containing 0.3 wt.% YH2. Sixteen process-parameter combinations were established, and two specimens were fabricated for each combination. Laser power, scanning speed, and hatch spacing were selected as the investigated variables. Relative density, surface roughness, and Vickers hardness were evaluated using the entropy weight method combined with the weighted-sum method. On this basis, the microstructure of the specimens produced under the optimal process parameters was systematically characterized. The results showed that the influence of the investigated factors on overall forming quality followed the order: hatch spacing > laser power > scanning speed. The optimal process parameters were a laser power of 200 W, a scanning speed of 1100 mm/s, and a hatch spacing of 0.10 mm, under which the specimens exhibited superior overall forming quality. The addition of 0.3 wt.% YH2 did not significantly alter the dominant phase constitution of the alloy, but promoted α′ martensite refinement and weakened the texture through the in situ formation of Y2O3 nano-oxide particles.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及TC4（Ti-6Al-4V）的PBF-LB工艺优化及显微组织演变，但未提供拉伸或疲劳性能数据，与用户关注的力学及疲劳性能方向关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: No tensile or fatigue properties reported; the only mechanical metric is Vickers hardness, which is insufficient for the mechanical/fatigue focus.

summary_zh.motivation: 优化含0.3 wt.% YH2的PBF-LB成形TC4合金的工艺参数，提高整体成形质量。
summary_zh.method: 采用三因素四水平正交设计，结合熵权法和加权和法综合评价相对密度、表面粗糙度和维氏硬度。
summary_zh.result: 最优参数为激光功率200W、扫描速度1100mm/s、扫描间距0.10mm，YH2添加细化α′马氏体并削弱织构。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验制备并测试16组工艺参数下的试样，验证优化结果。

summary_en.motivation: To optimize the process parameters for powder bed fusion with a laser beam (PBF-LB) of TC4 alloy with 0.3 wt.% YH2 addition to achieve superior overall forming quality.
summary_en.method: A three-factor, four-level orthogonal design was conducted, and the entropy weight method combined with the weighted-sum method was used to evaluate relative density, surface roughness, and Vickers hardness.
summary_en.result: Optimal parameters (laser power 200 W, scanning speed 1100 mm/s, hatch spacing 0.10 mm) yielded the best forming quality; YH2 addition refined α′ martensite and weakened texture via in-situ Y2O3 nano-oxide particles.
summary_en.validation: Experimental fabrication and characterization (density, roughness, hardness, microstructure) of specimens for all 16 parameter combinations validated the optimization.

key_terms.en: powder bed fusion with laser beam (PBF-LB)

papers.title: Effect of high-temperature plasma immersion ion implantation on the microstructure and hardness of laser beam-welded Ti-6Al-4V alloy
papers.abstract: Ti-6Al-4V welded joints remain challenging for thermochemical surface engineering because laser welding produces spatially heterogeneous microstructures and residual stress states, which can strongly affect diffusion and compound-layer formation during subsequent treatments. This study investigates the combined use of laser beam welding (LBW) and high-temperature nitrogen plasma immersion ion implantation (HT-PIII) as a surface engineering route for Ti-6Al-4V alloy joints. LBW was deliberately employed as a metallurgical pre-conditioning step, generating fusion and heat-affected zones with distinct microstructural features and stress conditions. Bead-on-plate welds were produced using a continuous-wave Yb:fiber laser under three nominal heat inputs (25, 50, and 75 J/mm), followed by HT-PIII treatment at 820 °C using a pulsed high-voltage discharge operating at 56 kV, with a pulse width of 30 μs and a repetition frequency of 1 kHz. The treated joints were characterized by X-ray diffraction, optical and scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive spectroscopy, Vickers microhardness, and instrumented hardness testing. The results showed the formation of a TiN/Ti2N-containing compound layer and a subsurface nitrogen diffusion zone, with thickness and chemical gradients dependent on the local metallurgical condition imposed by welding. The fusion zone exhibited greater nitrogen incorporation and a thicker implanted layer than the base material, reflecting its refined microstructure and higher defect density. Instrumented hardness measurements revealed pronounced near-surface hardening, with values exceeding 1800 HVIT in the implanted layer, whereas Vickers microhardness profiles indicated moderate hardness reductions in internal regions, likely associated with thermally induced microstructural changes during the HT-PIII thermal cycle. These findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of HT-PIII on Ti-6Al-4V joints cannot be dissociated from the prior welding condition. Rather than acting as an isolated surface treatment, HT-PIII interacts with the thermal and metallurgical state imposed by LBW, leading to spatially dependent surface modification while preserving the mechanical integrity of the welded joint.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是激光焊接Ti-6Al-4V合金后的高温等离子体浸没离子注入处理，而非增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理，因此与用户关注方向不相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on laser beam welded joints of Ti-6Al-4V, not additive manufactured material, and examines surface hardness rather than fatigue or mechanical performance relevant to AM post-processing control.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究激光焊接后等离子体浸没离子注入对Ti-6Al-4V焊接接头微观组织和硬度的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用不同热输入的激光焊接，随后进行高温氮等离子体浸没离子注入处理。
summary_zh.result: 形成TiN/Ti2N化合物层和氮扩散区，表面硬度超过1800 HVIT，但内部硬度降低。
summary_zh.validation: 通过XRD、SEM、EDS、维氏硬度和仪器化硬度测试验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the combined effect of laser beam welding and high-temperature plasma immersion ion implantation on the microstructure and hardness of Ti-6Al-4V joints.
summary_en.method: Bead-on-plate welds were produced with three heat inputs using a Yb:fiber laser, followed by HT-PIII treatment at 820 °C with pulsed high-voltage discharge.
summary_en.result: A TiN/Ti2N compound layer and nitrogen diffusion zone formed, with near-surface hardness exceeding 1800 HVIT and internal hardness reductions due to thermal effects.
summary_en.validation: Characterization by XRD, optical and scanning electron microscopy, EDS, Vickers microhardness, and instrumented hardness testing.
